title: The last day of school is nearing for Richland County students - NewsBreak
text:
By Zach Tuggle ,
20 hours ago The 2026 school year is nearly over for Richland County students.
Here's a look at what dates area school districts are planning for the last day of class:
Pioneer Career & Technology Center Last day of class: Friday, May 29
Shelby City Schools Last day of class: Wednesday, May 27
Ontario Local Schools Last day of class: Thursday, May 28
Galion City Schools Last day of class for seniors: Tuesday, May 12
Last day of class for grades K-11: Friday, May 22
Lexington Local Schools Last day of class: Tuesday, June 2
Mansfield City Schools Last day of class: Tuesday, June 2
Crestline Exempted Schools Last day of class for seniors: Friday, May 15
Last day of class for grades K-11: Thursday, May 21
Plymouth-Shiloh Local Schools Last day of class: Thursday, May 28
Clear Fork Valley Local Schools Last day of class: Thursday, May 28
Madison Local Schools Last day of class for seniors and elementary students: Friday, May 22
Last day of class for grades 5-11: Thursday, May 28
Crestview Local Schools Last day of class: Thursday, May 21
Lucas Local Schools Last day of class: Thursday, May 28
More: How much school will students make up? Districts waiting for state
How much school do students have to attend? A decade ago, ahead of the 2014-15 school year, the Ohio State Board of Education changed its regulation of instructional time from "days" to "hours."
Schools are bound by Ohio law when it comes to providing a minimum number of instructional hours each year, said Lacey Snoke, chief communications officer for the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce.
"Many schools and districts proactively build additional hours into their school-year calendars to meet these requirements, even when unexpected closures occur," Snoke said. "If closures cause a school to fall below the required number of hours, the school must extend its scheduled year."
The normal yearly state requirement is 455 hours for preschool, 910 hours for grades K-6 and 1,001 hours for grades 7-12.
"As an alternative, schools and districts may implement approved plans to make up hours through online learning," Snoke said. "These plans allow schools to replace the equivalent of up to three school days when closures occur due to allowable circumstances, including hazardous weather conditions."
